title: On-policy Distillation with Verifiable Reward
data_curation: No new data is built; the paper reuses public math RLVR sets with rule-based answer verification. Same-architecture setting: the filtered DeepMath subset of 57k problems with difficulty level >= 6 (following ExOPD), used both to train the teacher (Qwen3-4B trained with GRPO on DeepMath) and for distillation. Cross-architecture setting: DAPO-Math-17k, used to train the teacher (Qwen3-4B-Base, GRPO for 3 epochs) and for 3 epochs of distillation. The GRPD experiment deliberately distills on DAPO-Math-17K, distinct from the teacher's DeepMath training data. The verifier gives a trajectory-level reward R in {+1, -1} (OPDVR) or {0, 1} (GRPO-style group advantages in GRPD).
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. The pipeline is two-step by construction: first a same-size or larger teacher is obtained by GRPO on the math set (Qwen3-4B-RL or Qwen3-4B-Base-RL), then the student (Qwen3-4B-nonthinking or Qwen3-1.7B-Base) is trained with a single on-policy distillation stage (OPDVR or GRPD); there is no warmup, mixing schedule, or multi-stage student curriculum.
method: OPDVR reinterprets sampled-token OPD as RLVR: the stop-gradient log-ratio acts as an implicit token reward R_OPD = log(pi_T/pi_theta), whose sign depends on teacher-student confidence rather than correctness, so correct trajectories can be penalized (pi_theta > pi_T) and incorrect ones rewarded (pi_T > pi_theta). OPDVR applies a ReLU gate: correct trajectories get max(0, log(pi_T/pi_theta)), incorrect ones get -max(0, log(pi_theta/pi_T)); loss = -sum_t R_OPDVR(o_t) log pi_theta(o_t). This is a conditional token mask that removes the verifier-conflicting component of the OPD gradient (Prop. C.2), adds no hyperparameters, and under a soft-value-teacher assumption a gated mirror step never lowers task success and does not raise teacher KL for step size <= 1/2. GRPD replaces the binary sign with the sign of the GRPO group advantage (G=8). Built on verl: LR 1e-6, batch 256, PPO mini-batch 256, max response 8192, rollout temperature 1.0.
eval_metrics: Six math benchmarks (AIME24, AIME25, AMC, MATH500, Minerva, OlympiadBench), avg@16 accuracy at temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95. Same-architecture (Qwen3-4B <- Qwen3-4B-RL) average: student 42.0, teacher 50.4, sampled-token OPD 47.8, Top-64 OPD 47.4, OPD+GRPO 47.7, RLSD 44.8, ExOPD 47.9, SG-OPD 47.5, OPDVR 49.1 (AIME24 36.9, above the teacher's 36.0). Cross-architecture (Qwen3-1.7B-Base <- Qwen3-4B-Base-RL) average: OPD 20.9, best baseline Top-64 OPD 21.7, OPDVR 22.8. GRPD table average: GRPO 44.8, OPD 48.4, Distilled RL 48.7, GRPD 49.4. Training dynamics tracked: entropy, response length, and zero-gated token ratio (about 0.48-0.50 for 4B, 0.40-0.44 for 1.7B).
key_results: OPDVR raises the same-architecture average from 47.8 (sampled-token OPD) to 49.1, beating the next-best baseline ExOPD by 1.2 points, and lifts the cross-architecture average to 22.8 vs 21.7 for the best baseline; GRPD improves over GRPO by 6.5 points on AIME24 and 10.9 on AIME25 and over Distilled RL by 0.7 average. An inverse-gated ablation drops to 44.6 average, below vanilla OPD (47.8).
evolution_note: OPDVR sits in the 2026 wave of on-policy distillation (popularized by Qwen3, MiMo-V2-Flash, GLM-5 and DeepSeek-V4 post-training) and reacts to hybrids that combine OPD with RLVR via weighted losses or advantage-sign switching (OPD+GRPO, Distilled RL, RLSD) or trajectory/token-level conflict filters (Uni-OPD, RG-OPD, SG-OPD). Its contribution is showing that a hyperparameter-free sign gate turns sampled-token OPD into a proper RLVR objective, so it plugs into GRPO/DAPO/PPO and can in principle exceed the teacher rather than being capped by it.
